main_text.p: autem propria generis unius cujuspiā, ut Arithmetici, & Geometrae crediderūt, Διὰ τὴν τῶν ἀναλυτικῶν ἀπαιδευσίαν, propter analyticorum impe-ritiā. Hic Aristoteles mathematicos ut logicæ i-gnaros coarguit, quód logicam doctrinam non 5 exerceât, ut necesse erat, sed quód tanquam ma-thematicam aliquam in suis præceptis adnume-rent. Quin Aristoteles 5. cap. 1. Poster. eandē Lo-gicæ ἀπαιδευσίαν in mathematicis pari severitate reprehēdit, quód proportionum doctrinam in 10 mathematicis elementis permisceant. Itaq; Ari-stotelis ingeniū hac in re suspiciendū est, quód nobilissimæ disciplinæ confusionem tantā de-prehenderit, & quomodo vitanda esset, tam stu-diosé admonuerit. Videbat nimirum philoso-phus, si ad difficultatem rerū mathematicarum, etiam doctrinę cōfusio & obscuritas accederet, fore, ut hæc studia jacerent, ut postea tot secula jacuerunt: ut neque quisquam adhuc inventus sit, qui septimus post Hippocraté, Leonté, Theu-15 dium, Hermotimum, Euclidem, Theonem, ele-menta commodiùs & luculentiùs explicare cō-tenderet. Itaque & P. Ramus singulari alacrita-te, Aristotelis illam in Philosophia & Posterio-ribus vocem, tanquam ad se præcipué pertinen-20 tem excepit, totumq; mathematico Aristotelæ agriculturæ studio dies noctesque sese dedidit. Testis vigiliarum & meditationum fui, ut sæpé difficultate rerū & labore pené obrutus, admo-neretur à me, ut sibi aliquando parceret, & qdr vix, ac ne vix quidem hominum millia tam mul-ta potuissent, id unum se ne speraret effecturū, 25 qui-

page.notes: The line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 are marginal line markers, not references. The Greek phrases in the text are printed in Greek and transcribed as closely as the scan allows; the first Greek phrase and the phrase after "Logicæ" are uncertain. The page is lightly foxed, and the last line is partly obscured. The words "Posteriorum" and similar were read as printed. The line numbers in the right margin are placed next to the text lines 5 through 30 and have been marked where they stand. The printed word "suspiciendū" is read as printed. Manuscript annotations on the spine edge are not transcribed.
